newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand dollar ends strongly, views mixed.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand dollar ends strongly, views mixed.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended a quiet Friday session strongly but views were mixed as to where the currency goes from here.
Kiwi finished at US$0.6934/41, up from 0.6927/34 at the open, having traded a 0.6929-40 range on the day. The Trade-Weighted Index ended at 68.68, up from 68.56.
"I'm a bull but not everyone here agrees me," said one Wellington dealer. "I just think the market is short. It's still short," he said.
"It's a technical thing more than anything. We get O'Neill's comments and the market shrugs it off, but I know he's been saying it for a long time," he said.
Goldman Sachs analyst Jim O'Neill earlier told Reuters the Kiwi was grossly overvalued, as he has been saying for the last 18 months.
There was a view that stops were in place around 0.6950 and if that broke, Kiwi could quite quickly motor up to 0.6970-80, but a range of 0.6930-60 was expected to contain the Kiwi overnight.

Next week, the market should have more information to get its teeth into, with the March quarter CPI due on Tuesday, balance of payments data on Wednesday and building data on Thursday. -- James Gray (64 9 302 1253)
